boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Clemson University
boards.description: A guide to the essential late-night food stops and study fuel for Clemson Tigers, from on-campus dining halls to downtown staples.

cards.title: The Ultimate Late-Night Tray
cards.subtitle: Tiger Boulevard
cards.notes: Order a Cook Out Tray with a milkshake; this drive-thru is a primary late-night destination for students after hours.
cards.short_summary: A Southern fast-food staple famous for its customizable trays and 40+ milkshake flavors, open until 3:30 AM or later.
cards.evidence_claim: Cook Out is open Sunday-Thursday until 3:30 AM and Friday-Saturday until 4:30 AM.
cards.source_title: Best Drunk Food: Cook Out - The Tiger
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:30 AM (Sun-Thu) and 4:30 AM (Fri-Sat).

cards.title: Downtown Pizza Slices
cards.subtitle: Sloan Street
cards.notes: Grab a New York-style slice downtown; it is a frequent stop for students looking for a quick meal late into the night.
cards.short_summary: A popular downtown pizzeria serving New York-style pies and slices, known for its late-night availability near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Todaro Pizza is open until 3:00 AM daily.
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM daily.

cards.title: Warm Cookie Delivery
cards.subtitle: Fendley Street
cards.notes: Order warm cookies for delivery or pickup during late-night study sessions; a favorite for satisfying sweet cravings.
cards.short_summary: A bakery specializing in warm cookie delivery, catering specifically to the late-night college crowd.
cards.evidence_claim: Insomnia Cookies in Clemson offers pickup and delivery until 2:35 AM.
cards.access_notes: Open until approximately 2:35 AM for late-night service.

cards.title: 24/7 Diner Classics
cards.subtitle: Tiger Boulevard
cards.notes: Visit for scattered, smothered, and covered hashbrowns at any hour; a reliable 24-hour option for students.
cards.short_summary: The quintessential 24-hour American diner chain, providing breakfast and comfort food at all hours of the night.
cards.evidence_claim: Waffle House locations in Clemson are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7.

cards.title: East Campus Late Dining
cards.subtitle: Bryan Mall
cards.notes: Use a meal swipe for a late dinner on the east side of campus; known for its dessert selection and fireplace lounge.
cards.short_summary: One of Clemson's main residential dining halls, serving the East Campus community with various food stations.
cards.evidence_claim: Schilletter Dining Hall is open until 9:00 PM on most weeknights.
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM (Mon-Thu).

cards.title: Core Campus Fuel
cards.subtitle: McAlister Hall
cards.notes: Head to 'Core' for a late-night meal swipe; the second-level lounge is a popular spot for evening study groups.
cards.short_summary: A centrally located dining hall offering diverse stations including sushi, vegan options, and homestyle meals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dish at McAlister is open until 9:00 PM on most weeknights.
cards.source_title: The Dish at McAlister - Location Details
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM (Mon-Thu).

cards.title: The Hub at Douthit
cards.subtitle: Douthit Hills
cards.notes: Visit the newest dining hall for pizza or international fusion dishes; a key evening hub for Douthit Hills residents.
cards.short_summary: A modern all-you-care-to-eat dining facility located within the Douthit Hills residential complex.
cards.evidence_claim: The Community Hub at Douthit Hills operates until 9:00 PM Monday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Best Dining Hall: Douthit Hills Community Hub - The Tiger
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 PM (Mon-Thu).

cards.title: Late-Night Chicken Fingers
cards.subtitle: McAlister Hall
cards.notes: Grab a Box Combo with extra Cane's Sauce; this on-campus retail spot stays open later than the main dining halls.
cards.short_summary: A popular retail dining option on campus specializing in chicken fingers, crinkle-cut fries, and Texas toast.
cards.evidence_claim: Raising Cane's on campus is open until 12:00 AM on several weeknights.
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 AM on select nights (Tue-Thu).

cards.title: Custom Blended Treats
cards.subtitle: North Clemson Avenue
cards.notes: Enjoy custom-blended ice cream or a latte in a relaxed atmosphere; a popular non-bar late-night hangout.
cards.short_summary: A local coffee and ice cream shop known for its custom mix-ins and cozy seating, ideal for late-night studying.
cards.evidence_claim: Spill the Beans is open until 10:00 PM every night.
cards.source_title: Best Ice Cream: Andee's - The Tiger
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM daily.

cards.title: Midnight Study Snacks
cards.subtitle: Sigma Drive
cards.notes: Pick up energy drinks or snacks while studying at the library; conveniently located for late-night academic sessions.
cards.short_summary: A convenience market located at the main entrance of R.M. Cooper Library, providing essentials for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The P.O.D. Market at Cooper Library is open until Midnight Sunday through Thursday.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spot and P.O.D. Market: Cooper Library - The Tiger
cards.access_notes: Open until Midnight (Sun-Thu).

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study hubs and quiet retreats where Clemson students actually spend their time between classes and during late-night sessions.

cards.title: The Silent Zone
cards.subtitle: R.M. Cooper Library
cards.notes: Head to the second floor for strictly silent study. It features large wooden tables preserved from the original Sikes Hall library for a traditional academic feel.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent study floor in the main campus library featuring historic wooden tables.
cards.evidence_claim: The second floor of Cooper Library is a silent study space featuring wooden tables preserved from the original library in Sikes Hall.
cards.access_notes: Open late during semesters; silent study rules strictly enforced.

cards.title: The Collaborative Hub
cards.subtitle: Hendrix Student Center
cards.notes: Located on the first floor of Hendrix, this space offers seven closed-door rooms for group work. No reservations are required for these collaborative pods.
cards.short_summary: A modern collaborative study space on the first floor of the Hendrix Student Center with group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tiger Den in Hendrix Student Center features five 5-person and two 10-person closed-door collaborative rooms with no reservations necessary.
cards.source_title: Hendrix Student Center | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Open until 11:00 PM daily.

cards.title: The Sustainable Retreat
cards.subtitle: Lee Hall III
cards.notes: Visit this 30,000-square-foot green roof for a quiet outdoor break. The building is zero-energy ready and designed as a 'building that teaches.'
cards.short_summary: A massive rooftop garden atop the sustainable Lee Hall III building used for quiet outdoor study.
cards.evidence_claim: Lee III features a 30,000-square-foot roof garden and is referred to as the 'building that teaches.'
cards.access_notes: Access may be restricted to students with classes in the building during certain hours.

cards.title: The Tech Hub
cards.subtitle: Watt Family Innovation Center
cards.notes: Use the flexible seating and high-tech displays in the atrium for project work. It is a central hub for Creative Inquiry and interdisciplinary research.
cards.short_summary: A high-tech atrium with flexible seating and digital displays for collaborative student projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Watt Family Innovation Center offers flexible space for collaboration and project development for students in all disciplines.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday until 10:00 PM.

cards.title: The Open Lounge
cards.subtitle: Brackett Hall
cards.notes: Find this open computer lab and lounge area on the bottom floor. It is a reliable spot for walk-in study sessions without needing a reservation.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor atrium in Brackett Hall providing an open computer lab and lounge for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brackett Hall Atrium is located on the bottom floor and includes an open computer lab and lounge area with no reservations necessary.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday until 11:00 PM.

cards.title: The Connecting Bridge
cards.subtitle: Humanities Hall
cards.notes: Study on the bridge connecting the new additions to Daniel Hall. It offers modern collaborative seating and views of the central campus pedestrian routes.
cards.short_summary: A modern architectural bridge connecting campus buildings that serves as a collaborative study area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Humanities Hall expansion includes a connecting collaborative bridge that facilitates connectivity and provides study space.
cards.source_title: Clemson Daniel Hall - Lord Aeck Sargent
cards.access_notes: Open during general building hours, typically until 8:00 PM on weekdays.

cards.title: The Focus Rooms
cards.subtitle: Academic Success Center
cards.notes: Reserve a private room here for intense focus. The center also offers academic coaching and peer-assisted learning sessions to help you stay on track.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated facility for student support featuring reservable individual and group study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Success Center offers reservable individual and group study rooms from 7:30 a.m. to 10 p.m. on weekdays.
cards.access_notes: Reservations recommended; open Sunday evenings for late study.

cards.entity_name: Powers College of Business Hill Climb
cards.title: The Spanish Steps of Clemson
cards.subtitle: Powers College of Business
cards.notes: Modeled after Rome's Spanish Steps, this terraced exterior stair and plaza connects Bowman Field to Douthit Hills, perfect for outdoor socializing.
cards.short_summary: A dramatic terraced outdoor staircase and plaza designed for student connection and campus navigation.
cards.evidence_claim: The design of the Powers College of Business envisioned the hill climb as a defining feature akin to Rome's Spanish Steps.
cards.source_title: Clemson University Wilbur O. and Ann Powers College of Business
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor space accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Memorial Green
cards.subtitle: Near Sikes Hall
cards.notes: Relax in this picturesque green space dedicated by the Class of 1943. It is a quiet spot for reflection and small outdoor gatherings between classes.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful memorial garden located in the heart of campus near the administrative buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carillon Garden is a picturesque green space dedicated by the Class of 1943 as a tribute to those who lost their lives during WWII.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; outdoor public space.

cards.title: The 295-Acre Sanctuary
cards.subtitle: Perimeter Road
cards.notes: Escape the campus bustle at this massive sanctuary. It is free to the public and offers miles of trails and the Bob Campbell Geology Museum.
cards.short_summary: A sprawling botanical garden and research facility located on the edge of the Clemson campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The South Carolina Botanical Garden is a 295-acre sanctuary open and free of charge 365 days a year from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Explore Clemson's best social and recreational spots that require no admission or purchase, from lakeside retreats to campus galleries.

cards.title: Stroll the Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: 295-acre garden and nature preserve
cards.notes: Explore diverse plant life and themed landscapes across 295 acres. The grounds are open and free to the public 365 days a year from sunrise to sunset.
cards.short_summary: A massive, free public garden featuring trails, landscapes, and unique plant exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The South Carolina Botanical Garden grounds are open and free of charge 365 days a year from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. No admission fee required for self-guided visits.

cards.title: View the Geology Collection
cards.subtitle: Museum with 10,000+ specimens
cards.notes: Examine thousands of rocks, minerals, and fossils. This museum is located within the Botanical Garden and offers free admission to all visitors.
cards.short_summary: A free museum housing a vast collection of minerals and fossils on the university grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bob Campbell Geology Museum offers free admission and is open Monday through Sunday, 10 am to 5 pm.
cards.source_title: Bob Campbell Geology Museum - Clemson University
cards.access_notes: Open daily 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Admission is free.

cards.title: Browse the Lee Gallery
cards.subtitle: Contemporary art in Lee Hall
cards.notes: Visit Lee Hall to see rotating exhibitions of regional and national artists. The gallery is a primary hub for visual arts on campus and is free to visit.
cards.short_summary: A campus art gallery showcasing student, faculty, and professional works with no entry fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The vast majority of Clemson Visual Arts events, including Lee Gallery exhibitions, remain free for the public.
cards.access_notes: Typically open Monday-Thursday 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM during exhibitions.

cards.entity_name: Snow Family Outdoor Fitness and Wellness Complex
cards.title: Relax at the Campus Beach
cards.subtitle: Lakefront recreation area
cards.notes: Head to the lakefront for beach volleyball or sunbathing. Access is free for students with a valid CUID; community access is available during summer.
cards.short_summary: A premier lakeside facility offering beach access and outdoor recreation for the Clemson community.
cards.evidence_claim: Students have access to the Snow Family Outdoor Fitness & Wellness Complex as part of their campus recreation fees (no additional per-visit cost).
cards.source_title: Snow Family Outdoor Fitness and Wellness Complex - Clemson University
cards.access_notes: Requires valid TigerOne ID for entry. Open hours vary by season.

cards.title: Lounge at Andy's
cards.subtitle: Lakeside student social space
cards.notes: Use the 16,000-square-foot facility's lounge space to study or socialize with lake views. Day-use items like yard games are available for free onsite.
cards.short_summary: A modern lakeside center with free social spaces and equipment for onsite use.
cards.evidence_claim: Andy's offers exceptional lounge space for students to study or relax and provides free day-use items for use onsite.
cards.source_title: Snow Family Outdoor Fitness and Wellness Complex - Clemson University
cards.access_notes: Open to students, faculty, and staff with CUID. Check seasonal hours.

cards.title: Collaborate at the Watt Center
cards.subtitle: High-tech collaborative hub
cards.notes: Gather in the atrium or flexible collaboration spaces of this tech-forward building. It is open to all students for project development and study.
cards.short_summary: A technologically advanced building offering free collaborative spaces for all disciplines.
cards.evidence_claim: The Watt Center is available for students and faculty in all disciplines as a flexible space for collaboration.
cards.source_title: Watt Family Innovation Center - Clemson University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 7:30 AM to 10:00 PM, Friday until 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Study Late at Cooper Library
cards.subtitle: Main campus library
cards.notes: Access six floors of study space, including silent zones on lower levels. The library is the central hub for late-night academic sessions.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus library offering various study environments and late-night access.
cards.evidence_claim: Cooper Library offers late-night open study and a variety of individual and group seating options.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/5 during fall/spring semesters for students with CUID. Public access restricted.

cards.title: Listen to the Carillon
cards.subtitle: Outdoor musical tradition
cards.notes: Enjoy the sounds of the 48-bell carillon from this central campus garden. Annual events like 'Music in the Air' are free to attend.
cards.short_summary: A scenic campus garden where visitors can listen to live carillon performances for free.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual 'Music in the Air' tradition at the Carillon Garden is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor garden accessible 24/7; performances scheduled periodically.

cards.entity_name: Brooks Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Attend a Chamber Concert
cards.subtitle: Free professional music series
cards.notes: Experience world-class chamber music through the Utsey Series. These professional performances are free and open to the public, no tickets required.
cards.short_summary: A series of high-quality, professional chamber music concerts offered for free at the Brooks Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Utsey Chamber Music Series offers professional performances that are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Utsey Chamber Music Series - Clemson University
cards.access_notes: Performances typically held at 7:30 PM on select dates. Seating is first-come, first-served.

cards.title: Hike the Experimental Forest
cards.subtitle: 17,500-acre natural classroom
cards.notes: Explore over 100 miles of multi-use trails for hiking, running, or cycling. The forest is open to the public for recreation at no cost.
cards.short_summary: A vast university-managed forest providing extensive free trails for outdoor enthusiasts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clemson Experimental Forest offers more than 17,000 acres of land with trails and scenery open for public service and education.
cards.access_notes: Open daily for daylight use. Trail maps available online.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Choose ten distinct study environments. Verify access rules, room or reservation constraints, and the physical affordance that makes each useful. Treat “Claimed by 9am” as editorial framing; never assert crowding or student behavior without evidence.

cards.title: Silent Study Tables
cards.subtitle: R.M. Cooper Library
cards.notes: Utilize the large wooden tables preserved from the original Sikes Hall library for focused, silent work. This floor is designated for zero-talking productivity.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent study floor featuring historic wooden tables and a reflection room for meditation.
cards.evidence_claim: Floor 2 is a silent study space featuring large wooden tables preserved from the original library in Sikes Hall and a reflection room.
cards.access_notes: Open to students; floor 2 is strictly for silent study.

cards.title: Collaborative Atrium Seating
cards.subtitle: Watt Family Innovation Center
cards.notes: Find open seating and tables throughout the building for group projects. Reservable project rooms are available for more private team sessions.
cards.short_summary: A high-tech building offering flexible open study areas and reservable project rooms for collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: The Watt Family Innovation Center has tables and seats throughout the building available on a first-come, first-served basis and reservable project rooms.
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 7:30am-10:00pm, Friday 7:30am-5:00pm.

cards.title: Collaborative Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hendrix Student Center
cards.notes: Access closed-door collaborative rooms on the first floor. Five rooms seat five people, while two larger rooms accommodate ten and include screens.
cards.short_summary: A modern study space on the first floor of Hendrix featuring seven closed-door collaborative rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tiger Den on the first floor of Hendrix includes five 5-person and two 10-person closed-door collaborative rooms with screens.
cards.source_title: Where can I find study spaces and group meeting rooms on campus? - Library FAQ
cards.access_notes: No reservations necessary; open during Hendrix Student Center hours.

cards.title: Individual Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Academic Success Center
cards.notes: Reserve a private room equipped with a small whiteboard for focused individual work. Open seating is also available in the building's common areas.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated academic support building offering reservable individual and group study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Success Center offers reservable individual study rooms with small whiteboards and open study areas.
cards.access_notes: Reservations recommended; open Monday-Friday 7:30am-4:30pm.

cards.title: Courtyard View Tables
cards.subtitle: Lee Hall
cards.notes: Sit at student-designed tables overlooking the courtyard or use the mid-century modern Barcelona chairs. Lower level carrels provide quiet individual space.
cards.short_summary: A specialized library in Lee Hall featuring designer furniture and quiet study carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gunnin Architecture Library features student-designed tables overlooking the courtyard and individual study carrels on the lower level.
cards.access_notes: Access may be restricted to students with classes in Lee Hall; open M-F 8:30am-4:30pm.

cards.title: Ground Floor Lounge
cards.subtitle: Brackett Hall
cards.notes: Use the open computer lab and lounge area on the bottom floor. Window tables offer views of the reflection pond and library.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor study area with a computer lab and lounge seating near the reflection pond.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brackett Hall Atrium includes an open computer lab and lounge area with no reservations necessary.
cards.source_title: Where can I find study spaces and group meeting rooms on campus? - Library FAQ
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 6:45am-11:00pm, Friday-Saturday 6:45am-7:15pm.

cards.entity_name: Wilbur O. and Ann Powers College of Business
cards.title: Natural Light Lounges
cards.subtitle: Powers College of Business
cards.notes: Study in a modern environment filled with natural light. The building features various couches, chairs, and designated study rooms.
cards.short_summary: A new academic building offering sunlit lounges and modern study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wilbur O. and Ann Powers College of Business features natural light, various couches, chairs, and designated study rooms.
cards.source_title: The Best Study Spots in Clemson - Her Campus
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; includes an on-site cafe.

cards.title: Collaboration Spaces
cards.subtitle: Humanities Hall
cards.notes: Utilize eight dedicated collaboration spaces located between Daniel Hall and Cooper Library. These spots are designed for students to congregate between classes.
cards.short_summary: Eight open collaboration areas located centrally between major academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: Humanities Hall includes eight collaboration spaces where students can study and congregate between classes.
cards.source_title: Where can I find study spaces and group meeting rooms on campus? - Library FAQ
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 7:30am-8:00pm, Sunday 12:00pm-6:00pm.

cards.title: Individual Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Vickery Hall
cards.notes: Find individual study carrels in a large study room or reserve small group spaces. After 4:30pm, seats are available on a first-come, first-served basis.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study location offering individual carrels and reservable small group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Vickery Hall has individual study carrels in a large study room and reservable small group spaces.
cards.access_notes: Reservable M-F 8:00am-4:30pm; open study available after 4:30pm.

cards.title: Adobe Digital Studio
cards.subtitle: R.M. Cooper Library
cards.notes: Work in a collaborative environment featuring the Adobe Digital Studio and Makerspace. This floor allows for low talking and group work.
cards.short_summary: A creative study floor featuring digital design tools and a collaborative atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Floor 5 of Cooper Library features the Adobe Digital Studio, Makerspace, and allows for low talking/group study.
cards.access_notes: Open during library hours; includes an on-site Starbucks.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Clemson University, from the historic downtown core to the lakeside parks and student residential hubs.

cards.title: The Downtown Core
cards.subtitle: College Avenue Corridor
cards.notes: Walk the main artery connecting campus to downtown. It is the primary hub for student-focused dining, bookstores, and the famous Tiger paw-printed sidewalks.
cards.short_summary: The central commercial street of downtown Clemson, directly adjacent to the university's northern edge.
cards.evidence_claim: College Avenue is the main street which leads to Clemson University and cuts directly through the downtown area, housing many restaurants, coffee shops, and businesses.
cards.source_title: Life In Clemson – Graduate Student Organization
cards.access_notes: Public street; most businesses open daily from 10:00 AM to late evening.

cards.title: The Retail Corridor
cards.subtitle: U.S. Highway 123
cards.notes: Visit this major thoroughfare for essential retail, grocery stores like Publix, and a high concentration of national and local quick-service dining options.
cards.short_summary: A high-traffic commercial corridor perpendicular to College Avenue featuring major retail and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Tiger Boulevard (US-123) is the chain-hotel corridor and features many restaurants and places for quick food stops, including the Publix-anchored Gateway Village.
cards.access_notes: Major public highway; retail hours typically 7:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

cards.title: The Historic Side Street
cards.subtitle: Sloan Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore this historic block behind College Avenue, home to local boutiques like Sassy's and the long-standing Sloan Street Tap Room.
cards.short_summary: A quieter downtown street known for local boutiques and historic student hangouts.
cards.evidence_claim: Sloan Street is located in downtown Clemson and features local businesses such as Sassy's Boutique and the historic Sloan Street Tap Room.
cards.access_notes: Public street; boutique hours vary, typically 11:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

cards.title: The West Campus Gateway
cards.subtitle: SC Highway 93
cards.notes: Access the western edge of campus along this corridor, which features student housing complexes and local favorites like Gotta Run Clemson.
cards.short_summary: A major east-west thoroughfare serving the western residential and athletic areas of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Greenville Highway serves as a major E-W thoroughfare and is home to student housing like Fort Hill Commons and retail like Gotta Run Clemson.
cards.access_notes: Public highway; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Local Dining Block
cards.subtitle: Earle Street Corridor
cards.notes: Find a high density of student-favorite cafes on this block, including All In Coffee Shop and the popular Backstreets Pub & Deli.
cards.short_summary: A downtown side street famous for its concentration of local coffee shops and delis.
cards.evidence_claim: Earle Street in downtown Clemson is home to All In Coffee Shop and Backstreets Pub & Deli, popular spots for students to eat and study.
cards.access_notes: Public street; coffee shops often open early at 7:00 AM.

cards.title: The Pub District
cards.subtitle: Keith Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this block for local favorites like Grace Coffee Company and the Keith Street Pub, known for its extensive collection of Clemson memorabilia.
cards.short_summary: A small downtown street featuring a mix of coffee shops and local pubs.
cards.evidence_claim: Keith Street is home to Grace Coffee Company and the Keith Street Pub & Grille, which features Clemson memorabilia and a local atmosphere.
cards.access_notes: Public street; businesses typically open from 11:00 AM to late night.

cards.title: The New Urbanist Hub
cards.subtitle: Patrick Square Town Center
cards.notes: Explore the walkable Patrick Square district, featuring the Clemson Farmers Market and the Osher Lifelong Learning Institute.
cards.short_summary: The main boulevard of Patrick Square, a master-planned community three miles from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Thomas Green Boulevard is the heart of Patrick Square Town Center, hosting the Clemson Farmers Market and the Osher Lifelong Learning Institute (OLLI).
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible town center; Farmers Market held seasonally on Fridays.

cards.title: The Student Residential Corridor
cards.subtitle: Elm Street District
cards.notes: Walk through this major off-campus housing hub, home to large complexes like The District at Clemson and Riverbank Commons.
cards.short_summary: A primary residential street for off-campus students located south of Tiger Boulevard.
cards.evidence_claim: Elm Street is a major student housing corridor featuring developments like The District at Clemson and Riverbank Commons.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; accessible 24/7.

cards.title: The Lakeside Boardwalk
cards.subtitle: Keowee Trail Corridor
cards.notes: Enjoy the wooden boardwalks along Lake Hartwell. This park connects to the Keowee Trail and is a popular spot for sunset walks and waterfront views.
cards.short_summary: A scenic waterfront park and boardwalk located just off the downtown commercial district.
cards.evidence_claim: Abernathy Park features wooden boardwalks along and over Lake Hartwell and is a key recreation spot near downtown.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM.

cards.title: The Downtown Residential Pocket
cards.subtitle: Strode Circle Corridor
cards.notes: Discover this small residential pocket directly adjacent to downtown, known for its walkable proximity to the university and local pharmacies.
cards.short_summary: A compact residential and professional street located just off College Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Strode Circle is a residential area adjacent to College Avenue and Hubbard Young Pharmacy, featuring small apartment buildings and cottages.
cards.access_notes: Public residential street; accessible 24/7.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and symbols that define the Clemson Family, from rubbing a rock for luck to spending stamped currency at away games.

cards.title: Rubbing Howard's Rock
cards.subtitle: A piece of Death Valley, California
cards.notes: Touch the quartzite rock at the top of The Hill before football games. It was a gift to Coach Frank Howard in 1966 and became a 110% effort ritual in 1967.
cards.short_summary: A ritual where football players rub a pedestal-mounted rock for luck before running down The Hill.
cards.evidence_claim: The rock was first placed on a pedestal in 1966 and players began rubbing it for luck in 1967 after Coach Howard told them they must give 110% to touch it.
cards.access_notes: Visible at the east end zone of Memorial Stadium during games and stadium tours.

cards.title: Spending Stamped $2 Bills
cards.subtitle: A show of economic impact
cards.notes: Stamp $2 bills with orange Tiger Paws to spend at away games. This tradition started in 1977 to prove the financial impact of Clemson fans in Atlanta.
cards.short_summary: A tradition of using stamped $2 bills at away games to demonstrate the economic power of the Clemson Family.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition began in 1977 when fans used stamped $2 bills in Atlanta to show merchants the impact of Clemson's presence after a scheduling dispute with Georgia Tech.
cards.source_title: The $2 Dollar Bill Tradition - Clemson University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Practiced by fans traveling to away games; stamps are often available through the Alumni Association.

cards.title: Wearing Solid Orange
cards.subtitle: Every Friday is Orange Friday
cards.notes: Wear Clemson orange every Friday to show unity and pride. Launched in 1999, this tradition signals the start of the weekend for Tigers everywhere.
cards.short_summary: A weekly campus-wide event where students and staff wear orange to demonstrate school spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Solid Orange was launched in 1999 as a campaign to promote pride and unity, centered on wearing orange on Fridays and at athletic events.
cards.access_notes: Observed campus-wide every Friday throughout the year.

cards.title: The Rat Cap Wave
cards.subtitle: A nod to military history
cards.notes: Wave your hand with the thumb tucked under during the Alma Mater. This mimics the historical practice of cadets waving their 'rat caps' in the air.
cards.short_summary: A specific hand gesture performed during the singing of the university's Alma Mater.
cards.evidence_claim: The salute dates back to Clemson's military days when freshmen (rats) waved their caps; today, fans wave their hands as if holding a cap.
cards.access_notes: Performed at the conclusion of the Alma Mater at sporting events and ceremonies.

cards.title: Tigerama Pep Rally
cards.subtitle: One of the nation's largest student-run rallies
cards.notes: Attend this massive Homecoming pep rally featuring skits, fireworks, and the crowning of Miss Homecoming. It has been a Friday night staple since 1957.
cards.short_summary: An annual student-led pep rally held on the Friday night of Homecoming weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: Tigerama began in 1957 and is currently the second-largest fully student-run pep rally in the United States.
cards.access_notes: Held annually at Memorial Stadium during Homecoming week; tickets are required.

cards.title: The First Friday Parade
cards.subtitle: Kicking off the football season
cards.notes: Watch the parade along Highway 93 on the Friday before the first home game. This tradition has signaled the start of football season since 1974.
cards.short_summary: A community parade held on the first Friday of the football season to celebrate the team's return.
cards.evidence_claim: The First Friday Parade has been held since 1974 and proceeds along Highway 93 to a pep rally at Riggs Field.
cards.source_title: Clemson Experience | Welcome Week | Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: Free to watch along the parade route on Highway 93.

cards.title: Engraving the Sidewalks
cards.subtitle: Leaving a permanent legacy
cards.notes: Look for the names of over 53,000 alumni engraved in the concrete paths. This tradition began in the 1950s as a way for seniors to fund campus walkways.
cards.short_summary: A tradition where graduating seniors have their names engraved into campus sidewalks.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition started in the 1950s when seniors raised money for sidewalks; today, over 53,000 names are engraved across campus.
cards.access_notes: Engraved bricks are visible on sidewalks throughout the main campus, particularly near the Hendrix Student Center.

cards.title: Painting the Paws
cards.subtitle: Orange prints on the pavement
cards.notes: Spot the orange Tiger Paws painted on the roads leading into campus. City officials and students freshen the paint annually before the school year begins.
cards.short_summary: The practice of painting orange tiger paw logos on the streets of the town and campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition began unofficially in 1970 and is now an annual event where city officials freshen the paws on Highway 93 and other roads.
cards.source_title: Landmarks & Legends: Tiger Paw Prints - Clemson World Archive
cards.access_notes: Visible on public roads throughout the city of Clemson and the university campus.

cards.title: Building the Floats
cards.subtitle: Chicken wire and tissue paper
cards.notes: Visit Bowman Field during Homecoming week to see student organizations building massive, stationary floats using chicken wire and thousands of napkins.
cards.short_summary: A week-long tradition of constructing elaborate stationary displays on the campus's main field.
cards.evidence_claim: Student organizations gather on Bowman Field the week before the Homecoming game to build displays and a Habitat for Humanity house.
cards.access_notes: Displays are free to view on Bowman Field during Homecoming week.

cards.title: The Ring Flip
cards.subtitle: Facing the world
cards.notes: Wear your class ring with the date facing you until graduation, then flip it to face outward. This signifies your transition from student to alumnus.
cards.short_summary: A tradition involving the orientation of the Clemson class ring before and after graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Seniors wear the ring with the date facing them; at graduation, the ring is flipped so the date faces the world.
cards.access_notes: Ceremonies are held at the Littlejohn Coliseum; the flip occurs during the graduation ceremony.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Clemson University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide to starting your Clemson journey with campus traditions, late-night events, and essential student spots during your first weekend.

cards.title: Learn the Traditions at the Welcome Rally
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon Kickoff
cards.notes: Gather at the outdoor amphitheater to learn Clemson cheers and traditions with fellow new students during the official Welcome Rally.
cards.short_summary: An essential orientation event where new Tigers learn the school's famous chants and traditions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Welcome Rally is held on August 15 from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. at the Amphitheater to introduce new students to Clemson traditions.
cards.source_title: Weeks of Welcome | CSLE | Division of Student Affairs, Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: Open to all new students as part of the Weeks of Welcome programming.

cards.title: Late Night Laser Tag in the Ballrooms
cards.subtitle: Friday Night Fun
cards.notes: Head to the Hendrix Student Center ballrooms for a high-energy game of laser tag, a staple of the first-weekend late-night activities.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night social event featuring laser tag inside the student center's large ballrooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Laser Tag is scheduled for August 14 from 7 p.m. to 10 p.m. in the Hendrix Ballrooms as part of the Weeks of Welcome.
cards.source_title: Weeks of Welcome | CSLE | Division of Student Affairs, Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: Events typically run until 10 p.m. or 11 p.m. during the first weekend.

cards.title: Relax on the Historic Bowman Field
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning Chill
cards.notes: Join students on this iconic green space for frisbee, sunbathing, or studying in front of the historic Tillman Hall.
cards.short_summary: The central social hub of campus, perfect for outdoor recreation and meeting new people.
cards.evidence_claim: Bowman Field is a favorite spot for leisure activities and events, located between Tillman Hall and downtown Clemson.
cards.source_title: Things To Do in Clemson | Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible 24/7; most active during daylight hours.

cards.title: Taste Student-Made Clemson Ice Cream
cards.subtitle: Saturday Afternoon Treat
cards.notes: Visit this student-run shop in the Hendrix Student Center to try world-class ice cream manufactured by Clemson students.
cards.short_summary: A student-run enterprise serving famous ice cream made on-site by the Food, Nutrition and Packaging Sciences department.
cards.evidence_claim: '55 Exchange is a world-class ice cream shop located in the Hendrix Student Center, run entirely by students.
cards.source_title: Hendrix Student Center | CRE | Division of Student Affairs, Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Hendrix; check seasonal hours for weekend availability.

cards.title: Explore the Welcome Back Festival
cards.subtitle: Saturday Evening Downtown
cards.notes: Walk through downtown Clemson during this annual festival featuring local vendors, food, and student organization booths.
cards.short_summary: A massive street festival on College Avenue that welcomes students back to the town and campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Welcome Back Festival is the premiere kick-off event of the academic year, held in downtown Clemson.
cards.source_title: Weeks of Welcome: Weeks 1 | CSLE | Division of Student Affairs, Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: The festival typically takes place on the Saturday before classes begin.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot at Cooper
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning Prep
cards.notes: Explore the six floors of the main campus library to find your preferred volume level and grab a coffee at the on-site Starbucks.
cards.short_summary: The central academic hub of Clemson, offering diverse study environments and resources.
cards.evidence_claim: R.M. Cooper Library is the main campus library with six floors organized by volume and a Starbucks on the fourth floor.
cards.source_title: Best Study Spot and P.O.D. Market: Cooper Library - The Tiger
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid CUID for entry; open 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Saturdays and 1 p.m. to midnight on Sundays.

cards.title: Walk the Trails at the Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon Escape
cards.notes: Take a peaceful walk through 230 acres of gardens and natural heritage trails located right on the edge of campus.
cards.short_summary: A sprawling sanctuary featuring diverse plant collections, art galleries, and a geology museum.
cards.evidence_claim: The South Carolina Botanical Garden is open and free of charge 365 days a year from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; free admission for all visitors.

cards.title: Paint Pottery at the Barnes Center
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening Social
cards.notes: Join a creative session at the Barnes Center, a social hub located in a historic barn, for pottery painting and music.
cards.short_summary: A unique student social space that hosts creative workshops and late-night events.
cards.evidence_claim: Pottery Painting is held at the Barnes Center on August 16 from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m. as part of the Weeks of Welcome.
cards.source_title: Weeks of Welcome | CSLE | Division of Student Affairs, Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: The Barnes Center is a late-night social venue for students; check the schedule for specific workshop times.

cards.title: Late Night Breakfast at CORE
cards.subtitle: Sunday Night Tradition
cards.notes: Fuel up for the first day of classes with a late-night breakfast and trivia session at the CORE dining hall.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night dining event held at the CORE campus dining facility during the first week.
cards.evidence_claim: Breakfast Trivia with TigerLIVE is held at The Dish at McAlister (CORE Dining Hall) from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.source_title: Weeks of Welcome | CSLE | Division of Student Affairs, Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: Late-night hours for this event are 9 p.m. to 11 p.m.

cards.title: Attend University Convocation
cards.subtitle: Monday Morning Milestone
cards.notes: Join the entire freshman class in 'Death Valley' for the official academic welcome and to receive your first Clemson T-shirt.
cards.short_summary: The formal induction ceremony for new students, held in the iconic football stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: Convocation is the first step in a student's Clemson journey, where they learn the culture and receive free T-shirts in Memorial Stadium.
cards.source_title: Clemson Experience | Welcome Week | Clemson University, South Carolina
cards.access_notes: Held on the Monday morning before the first day of classes.
